runs.text: max-age, no-cache and no-store set three different cache contracts
max-age=N lets any cache reuse the response for N seconds without asking the origin.
no-cache still lets a cache store the response, but it must revalidate with the origin before every reuse.
no-store forbids keeping the response anywhere, so every request goes to the origin.
s-maxage overrides max-age for shared caches such as a CDN, leaving browsers on max-age.

slide.notes: no-cache is the one most often misread: it means revalidate, not do not cache.

arguments.source:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Cache
  participant O as Origin
  C->>O: GET /page
  O-->>C: 200 + ETag
  Note over C: copy goes stale
  C->>O: If-None-Match
  O-->>C: 304 Not Modified
arguments.caption: Revalidating a stale copy with its ETag

runs.text: An ETag turns a full re-download into a 304 Not Modified
The origin sends an ETag, a validator for this version of the response, alongside the body.
Once the cached copy is stale, the cache asks again with If-None-Match carrying that ETag.
If nothing changed, the origin answers 304 with no body and the cache keeps serving its copy.
If it changed, the origin sends 200 with the new body and a new ETag.

slide.notes: Revalidation saves the body transfer, not the round trip.

runs.text: A CDN serves stale content only where the headers allow it
stale-while-revalidate=N lets the CDN serve a stale copy for N seconds while it refetches in the background.
stale-if-error=N lets it serve the stale copy when the origin errors or cannot be reached.
Outside those windows a stale object must be revalidated before it is served.
Purging the object or setting a short s-maxage is how to keep stale content from users.

slide.notes: Both stale extensions are opt-in per response.

runs.text: An ETag turns a full re-download into a 304 Not Modified
The origin sends an ETag with the body: an opaque validator naming this exact version of the response.
While the copy is fresh, the cache serves it without asking; once it is stale, it must check before reuse.
To check, the cache sends the request again with If-None-Match carrying the ETag it holds.
If nothing changed, the origin answers 304 Not Modified with no body, and the cache keeps serving its copy with refreshed headers.
If it changed, the origin sends 200 with the new body and a new ETag, which replaces the stored copy.
The round trip remains; what revalidation saves is transferring the body again.

slide.notes: Revalidation saves the body transfer, not the round trip.

runs.text: A CDN serves stale content only where the headers allow it
While fresh, the CDN answers from its copy without contacting the origin.
stale-while-revalidate=N lets it serve the stale copy for N more seconds while it refetches in the background.
Outside that window a stale object must be revalidated before it is served.
stale-if-error=N lets it serve the stale copy when the origin errors or cannot be reached.
Purging the object or setting a short s-maxage is how to keep stale content from users.

slide.notes: Both stale extensions are opt-in per response.
